title: Tunneling characteristics of twisted double bilayer graphene heterostructures
authors: Alexey A. Sokolik, Azat F. Aminov, Evgenii E. Vdovin, Yurii N. Khanin, Mikhail A. Kashchenko, Denis A. Bandurin, Sergey V. Morozov, Kostya S. Novoselov
abstract: Electron tunneling between sheets of bilayer Bernal graphene twisted at different small angles was studied experimentally and theoretically. The current-voltage characteristics exhibit resonant peaks, steps, and regions of negative differential resistance, the origin of which is explained by the intersections of energy- and momentum-shifted electron dispersions of adjacent layers. A theoretical analysis of tunneling transport demonstrated that the key to understanding this phenomenon lies in the competition between two contributions: between like (conductivity-conductivity or valence-valence) and unlike (conductivity-valence) bands of parallel bilayer graphene sheets. A systematic evolution of the tunneling current patterns with increase of the twist angle is investigated. Polarization of electron wave function across graphene sublayers caused by displacement field within bilayer graphene is shown to strongly affect the tunneling probability, thus enhancing negative differential resistance due to Van Hove singularities at the band edges.
summary: This work experimentally and theoretically characterizes electron tunneling in twisted double bilayer graphene. It reveals that the observed current features, such as resonant peaks and steps, are governed by the interplay between like-band and unlike-band tunneling pathways. The results highlight that the symmetry and magnitude of these features are highly sensitive to the twist angle and the relative doping of the graphene layers.
main_problem: The study investigates the electron tunneling characteristics in twisted double bilayer graphene (BLG) heterostructures.
main_result: The tunneling current exhibits distinct features—resonant peaks and steps—whose nature (symmetric vs. asymmetric) depends critically on the relative doping levels and the twist angle.
method: The research combines experimental measurements of current-voltage (I-V) characteristics with detailed theoretical modeling based on electron dispersion intersections.
model_or_system: The system is a twisted double bilayer graphene heterostructure studied in a dual-gate architecture. The theory models tunneling current by considering the competition between like-band (conductivity-conductivity) and unlike-band (conductivity-valence) electron tunneling contributions.
key_observables: Current-voltage (I-V) characteristics, zero-bias tunneling conductance maps, resonant peaks, steps, and regions of negative differential resistance (NDR).
important_parameters: Twist angle ($	heta$), bias voltage ($V_b$), and relative doping levels (equal vs. opposite density).
main_assumptions: Tunneling transitions conserve lateral electron momentum and energy; the model incorporates the competition between different band types and the effect of sublayer polarization.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate I-V curves and 2D maps showing how tunneling features change with twist angle and doping asymmetry, distinguishing between symmetric and asymmetric regimes.
paper_structure: The paper systematically analyzes the tunneling current by decomposing it into like-band and unlike-band components, comparing theoretical predictions with experimental data across varying twist angles and doping conditions.
why_interesting: The strong dependence of tunneling features on band structure intersections and polarization effects provides a rich platform for studying quantum transport in engineered 2D materials, relevant to open quantum systems.
